paragraphs.text: and he stood upon the sand of the sea. And I saw a beast coming up out of the sea, having ten horns, and seven heads, and on his horns ten diadems, and upon his heads names of blasphemy.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἶδον ἐκ τῆς θαλάσσης θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον, ἔχον κέρατα δέκα καὶ κεφαλὰς ἑπτά, καὶ ἐπὶ τῶν κεράτων αὐτοῦ δέκα διαδήματα, καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτοῦ ὀνόματα βλασφημίας.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eidon ek tēs thalassēs thērion anabainon, echon kerata deka kai kephalas hepta, kai epi tōn keratōn autou deka diadēmata, kai epi tas kephalas autou onomata blasphēmias.

paragraphs.text: And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard, and his feet were as [the feet] of a bear, and his mouth as the mouth of a lion: and the dragon gave him his power, and his throne, and great authority.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδον ἦν ὅμοιον παρδάλει, καὶ οἱ πόδες αὐτοῦ ὡς ἄρκου, καὶ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ ὡς στόμα λέοντος. καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτῷ ὁ δράκων τὴν δύναμιν αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν θρόνον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξουσίαν μεγάλην.
paragraphs.translit: kai to thērion ho eidon ēn homoion pardalei, kai hoi podes autou hōs arkou, kai to stoma autou hōs stoma leontos. kai edōken autō ho drakōn tēn dynamin autou kai ton thronon autou kai exousian megalēn.

paragraphs.text: And [I saw] one of his heads as though it had been smitten unto death; and his death-stroke was healed: and the whole earth wondered after the beast;
paragraphs.original: καὶ μίαν ἐκ τῶν κεφαλῶν αὐτοῦ ὡς ἐσφαγμένην εἰς θάνατον, καὶ ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ ἐθεραπεύθη. καὶ ἐθαυμάσθη ὅλη ἡ γῆ ὀπίσω τοῦ θηρίου,
paragraphs.translit: kai mian ek tōn kephalōn autou hōs esphagmenēn eis thanaton, kai hē plēgē tou thanatou autou etherapeuthē. kai ethaumasthē holē hē gē opisō tou thēriou,

paragraphs.text: and they worshipped the dragon, because he gave his authority unto the beast; and they worshipped the beast, saying, Who is like unto the beast? And who is able to war with him?
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ δράκοντι ὅτι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ προσεκύνησαν τῷ θηρίῳ λέγοντες· Τίς ὅμοιος τῷ θηρίῳ, καὶ τίς δύναται πολεμῆσαι μετʼ αὐτοῦ;
paragraphs.translit: kai prosekynēsan tō drakonti hoti edōken tēn exousian tō thēriō, kai prosekynēsan tō thēriō legontes· Tis homoios tō thēriō, kai tis dynatai polemēsai metʼ autou;

paragraphs.text: and there was given to him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and there was given to him authority to continue forty and two months.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ στόμα λαλοῦν μεγάλα καὶ βλασφημίας, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ποιῆσαι μῆνας τεσσεράκοντα δύο.
paragraphs.translit: Kai edothē autō stoma laloun megala kai blasphēmias, kai edothē autō exousia poiēsai mēnas tesserakonta dyo.

paragraphs.text: And he opened his mouth for blasphemies against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, [even] them that dwell in the heaven.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤνοιξε τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ εἰς βλασφημίας πρὸς τὸν θεόν, βλασφημῆσαι τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν σκηνὴν αὐτοῦ, τοὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ σκηνοῦντας.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēnoixe to stoma autou eis blasphēmias pros ton theon, blasphēmēsai to onoma autou kai tēn skēnēn autou, tous en tō ouranō skēnountas.

paragraphs.text: And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them: and there was given to him authority over every tribe and people and tongue and nation.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι πόλεμον μετὰ τῶν ἁγίων καὶ νικῆσαι αὐτούς, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ἐξουσία ἐπὶ πᾶσαν φυλὴν καὶ λαὸν καὶ γλῶσσαν καὶ ἔθνος.
paragraphs.translit: kai edothē autō poiēsai polemon meta tōn hagiōn kai nikēsai autous, kai edothē autō exousia epi pasan phylēn kai laon kai glōssan kai ethnos.

paragraphs.text: And all that dwell on the earth shall worship him, [every one] whose name hath not been written from the foundation of the world in the book of life of the Lamb that hath been slain.
paragraphs.original: καὶ προσκυνήσουσιν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, οὗ οὐ γέγραπται τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ βιβλίῳ τῆς ζωῆς τοῦ ἀρνίου τοῦ ἐσφαγμένου ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
paragraphs.translit: kai proskynēsousin auton pantes hoi katoikountes epi tēs gēs, hou ou gegraptai to onoma autou en tō bibliō tēs zōēs tou arniou tou esphagmenou apo katabolēs kosmou.

paragraphs.text: If any man hath an ear, let him hear.
If any man [is] for captivity, into captivity he goeth: if any man shall kill with the sword, with the sword must he be killed. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.
paragraphs.original: εἴ τις εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν, εἰς αἰχμαλωσίαν ὑπάγει· εἴ τις ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι αὐτὸν ἐν μαχαίρῃ ἀποκτανθῆναι. ὧδέ ἐστιν ἡ ὑπομονὴ καὶ ἡ πίστις τῶν ἁγίων.
paragraphs.translit: ei tis eis aichmalōsian, eis aichmalōsian hypagei· ei tis en machairē apoktanthēnai auton en machairē apoktanthēnai. hōde estin hē hypomonē kai hē pistis tōn hagiōn.

paragraphs.text: And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like unto lamb, and he spake as a dragon.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἶδον ἄλλο θηρίον ἀναβαῖνον ἐκ τῆς γῆς, καὶ εἶχεν κέρατα δύο ὅμοια ἀρνίῳ, καὶ ἐλάλει ὡς δράκων.
paragraphs.translit: Kai eidon allo thērion anabainon ek tēs gēs, kai eichen kerata dyo homoia arniō, kai elalei hōs drakōn.

paragraphs.text: And he exerciseth all the authority of the first beast in his sight. And he maketh the earth and them dwell therein to worship the first beast, whose death-stroke was healed.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὴν ἐξουσίαν τοῦ πρώτου θηρίου πᾶσαν ποιεῖ ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ. καὶ ποιεῖ τὴν γῆν καὶ τοὺς ἐν αὐτῇ κατοικοῦντας ἵνα προσκυνήσουσιν τὸ θηρίον τὸ πρῶτον, οὗ ἐθεραπεύθη ἡ πληγὴ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai tēn exousian tou prōtou thēriou pasan poiei enōpion autou. kai poiei tēn gēn kai tous en autē katoikountas hina proskynēsousin to thērion to prōton, hou etherapeuthē hē plēgē tou thanatou autou.

paragraphs.text: And he doeth great signs, that he should even make fire to come down out of heaven upon the earth in the sight of men.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ποιεῖ σημεῖα μεγάλα, ἵνα καὶ πῦρ ποιῇ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνειν εἰς τὴν γῆν ἐνώπιον τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
paragraphs.translit: kai poiei sēmeia megala, hina kai pyr poiē ek tou ouranou katabainein eis tēn gēn enōpion tōn anthrōpōn.

paragraphs.text: And he deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by reason of the signs which it was given him to do in the sight of the beast; saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast who hath the stroke of the sword and lived.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πλανᾷ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς διὰ τὰ σημεῖα ἃ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ ποιῆσαι ἐνώπιον τοῦ θηρίου, λέγων τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ποιῆσαι εἰκόνα τῷ θηρίῳ, ὃς ἔχει τὴν πληγὴν τῆς μαχαίρης καὶ ἔζησεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai plana tous katoikountas epi tēs gēs dia ta sēmeia ha edothē autō poiēsai enōpion tou thēriou, legōn tois katoikousin epi tēs gēs poiēsai eikona tō thēriō, hos echei tēn plēgēn tēs machairēs kai ezēsen.

paragraphs.text: And it was given [unto him] to give breath to it, [even] to the image to the breast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as should not worship the image of the beast should be killed.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ δοῦναι πνεῦμα τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου, ἵνα καὶ λαλήσῃ ἡ εἰκὼν τοῦ θηρίου καὶ ποιήσῃ ἵνα ὅσοι ἐὰν μὴ προσκυνήσωσιν τῇ εἰκόνι τοῦ θηρίου ἀποκτανθῶσιν.
paragraphs.translit: kai edothē autō dounai pneuma tē eikoni tou thēriou, hina kai lalēsē hē eikōn tou thēriou kai poiēsē hina hosoi ean mē proskynēsōsin tē eikoni tou thēriou apoktanthōsin.

paragraphs.text: And he causeth all, the small and the great, and the rich and the poor, and the free and the bond, that there be given them a mark on their right hand, or upon their forehead;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ποιεῖ πάντας, τοὺς μικροὺς καὶ τοὺς μεγάλους, καὶ τοὺς πλουσίους καὶ τοὺς πτωχούς, καὶ τοὺς ἐλευθέρους καὶ τοὺς δούλους, ἵνα δῶσιν αὐτοῖς χάραγμα ἐπὶ τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῶν τῆς δεξιᾶς ἢ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῶν,
paragraphs.translit: kai poiei pantas, tous mikrous kai tous megalous, kai tous plousious kai tous ptōchous, kai tous eleutherous kai tous doulous, hina dōsin autois charagma epi tēs cheiros autōn tēs dexias ē epi to metōpon autōn,

paragraphs.text: and that no man should be able to buy or to sell, save he that hath the mark, [even] the name of the beast or the number of his name.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἵνα μή τις δύνηται ἀγοράσαι ἢ πωλῆσαι εἰ μὴ ὁ ἔχων τὸ χάραγμα, τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ θηρίου ἢ τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ ὀνόματος αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai hina mē tis dynētai agorasai ē pōlēsai ei mē ho echōn to charagma, to onoma tou thēriou ē ton arithmon tou onomatos autou.

paragraphs.text: Here is wisdom. He that hath understanding, let him count the number of the beast; for it is the number of a man: and his number is Six hundred and sixty and six.
paragraphs.original: ὧδε ἡ σοφία ἐστίν· ὁ ἔχων νοῦν ψηφισάτω τὸν ἀριθμὸν τοῦ θηρίου, ἀριθμὸς γὰρ ἀνθρώπου ἐστίν· καὶ ὁ ἀριθμὸς αὐτοῦ ἑξακόσιοι ἑξήκοντα ἕξ.
paragraphs.translit: hōde hē sophia estin· ho echōn noun psēphisatō ton arithmon tou thēriou, arithmos gar anthrōpou estin· kai ho arithmos autou hexakosioi hexēkonta hex.
